outcome: immune response (TLR4 route activation, pro-inflammatory cytokine release)
intestinal function (epithelial barrier function, intestinal maturation)
cohort: The study included 180 healthy infants, with 23 born at home and 157 born in hospital, 41.7% via cesarean section.
finding: Mode and place of birth influence the neonatal gut microbiota, shaping its interplay with the host's intestinal epithelium and immune system, which can affect metabolic processes and infant growth (e.g., higher BMI/W/L in C-section infants).
mod_finding: C-section delivery was associated with decreased Bacteroidetes and Bifidobacterium genus, higher BMI and W/L z-scores during the first 18 months, and distinct effects on epithelial barrier function, intestinal maturation, and immunological response compared to home birth.
